The ending feels entirely natural, purposeful, and earned. Throughout the story, the author builds themes of disorientation, collective motherhood ("Let's get you back to bed, Mom, as if it were our shared surname"), and the surreal strangeness of bringing a new person into the world. Details like the creased ear, the identical blankets, the parked bassinets, and the slipped ankle bands all carefully set up the climax in the car. The final moments—where the narrator accepts the switched baby with "plain and enormous" happiness and begins to see herself in the child ("it was true, or it was becoming true")—bring the story's emotional and thematic arcs to a resonant, satisfying resolution.
